svg.title: Cell biology overview
svg.desc: Cell structures: Nucleus: DNA and cell control. Cytoplasm: chemical reactions. Membrane: controls entry and exit. Mitochondria: aerobic respiration. Ribosomes: protein synthesis. Plants and algae: cellulose wall and permanent vacuole. Photosynthetic cells have chloroplasts. Bacteria: smaller, no nucleus, DNA loop. Some have plasmids. Specialised cells: Sperm: tail, mitochondria, acrosome enzymes. Nerve: long fibre and branches. Muscle: contractile proteins and mitochondria. Root hair: large absorption area. Xylem: hollow, lignified water tubes. Phloem: sugar transport and companion cells. Differentiation & stem cells: Differentiation: becoming specialised. Animals mainly early in life. Many plant cells can do this throughout life. Embryonic: most human cell types. Bone marrow: limited types. Meristems: any plant cell type. Uses: tissue repair and plant clones. Balance benefits, infection risk and ethics. Microscopy: Resolution: distinguish nearby points. Electron microscopes give greater magnification and finer detail. Magnification = image ÷ actual Use the same units. 1 mm = 1,000 µm. Slide: thin sample, stain, angled coverslip. Low power, focus, draw, label and a scale. Culturing microorganisms: Binary fission: repeated doubling. Population = start × 2ⁿ n = time ÷ division time Asepsis: sterilise equipment and cool the loop. Tape edges, invert plate, incubate at ≤25°C in school. Compare antimicrobial discs. Use a solvent control and repeats. Zone area = πr². Radius = diameter ÷ 2. Cell cycle: Grow → copy DNA → mitosis → divide Copies separate into two complete sets. Nuclei divide, then cytoplasm and membrane divide. Two identical cells: same chromosome number. For growth, development, repair and replacement. Diffusion & exchange: Diffusion: net movement from high to low concentration. No respiration energy. Faster with a steeper gradient, higher temperature or larger area. Large organisms have lower SA:V. Need exchange and transport systems. Cube: SA = 6a², volume = a³. Alveoli, villi and gills: large area, thin barrier and blood supply. Ventilation maintains gas gradients. Osmosis & transport: Osmosis: water moves from dilute to concentrated solution through a partially permeable membrane. Gain: plant turgid, animal swells. Loss: plant flaccid, animal shrinks. Practical: equal plant samples, weigh, soak, blot and reweigh. % change = (final − initial) ÷ initial × 100 Active transport: low to high concentration, using respiration energy. Examples: root mineral uptake and gut sugar absorption.
